decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent.

changes.quote: In support of its goals and in light of the shift in the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed adjusted its key interest rate downward to support the economy as employment risks increased.

changes.quote: The Committee decided to conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings on December 1.
changes.explanation: The central bank announced a specific end date for scaling back its bond holdings.

changes.quote: Available indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: The description of economic growth was updated to reflect current incoming data.

changes.quote: Job gains have slowed this year, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remained low through August; more recent indicators are consistent with these developments.
changes.explanation: Language was added to acknowledge slowing job gains and a slightly higher unemployment rate.

changes.quote: Voting against this action were Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point at this meeting, and Jeffrey R. Schmid, who preferred no change to the target range for the federal funds rate at this meeting.
changes.explanation: Two members dissented, with one preferring a larger cut and the other preferring no change at all.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months.
Inflation has moved up since earlier in the year and remains somewhat elevated.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 21.16% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.08% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.27% would rise by about $17.61 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.4%, and employers added an average of 23k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3% over the past year (September 2025); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.9% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +12 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.09% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate decisions will depend on incoming data regarding inflation and labor market conditions.
